explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/48: 'Are there infinitely many integers n, m such that φ(n) = σ(m)?' (yes, Ford–Luca–Pomerance [FLP10]: infinitely many common values). The statement asserts that the set of pairs (n, m) ∈ ℕ² with φ(n) = σ_1(m) is infinite. This is equivalent to infinitely many common values: each value a >= 1 has only finitely many n with φ(n) = a and finitely many m with σ(m) = a, so infinitely many pairs force infinitely many values, and the junk pair (0, 0) is a single element. The positive statement for an answered yes-question follows the upstream convention. Faithful.
